We partner with governments to recruit, train, equip, and integrate professional community health workers into national health systems, equipping them to deliver quality primary care in rural and remote communities. Founded in Liberia in 2007, we now operate programs in Ethiopia, Liberia, Sierra Leone, and Malawi. Our global offices are located in Accra, Ghana and in the United States. Led by Abraham Zerihun, the team works to upskill the Health Extension Workers through blended learning that combines digital and in-person training. The team's portfolio spans maternal, newborn, child health, nutrition, and non-communicable diseases, including hypertension, diabetes, eye care, and stroke prevention and management, while strengthening health systems through sustainable community health financing, resource mapping, and strategic planning to support long-term government leadership and program sustainability. The Role At Last Mile Health (LMH), we make bold commitments that inspire innovation. Team and Role Purpose Addis Ababa hosts the African Union (AU), one of the world’s most influential institutions, whose policies, frameworks, and decisions shape the lives of millions of children across the African continent. Through its normative, policy, and convening roles, the AU plays a critical part in advancing children's rights, promoting social justice, strengthening protection systems, and supporting sustainable development outcomes for children. Save the Children’s Global Diplomacy and Engagement Team in Addis Ababa serves as strategic gateway for engagement with AU institutions and other Pan-African stakeholders. The team works to influence regional policies, commitments, and accountability mechanisms to ensure that children's rights and wellbeing remain at the center of the AU agenda. This includes advancing priorities related to child protection, education, health, humanitarian action, participation, and children's rights in conflict and crisis settings. By building strong partnerships with AU departments, member states, civil society organizations, regional networks, and development partners, the team promotes evidence-based advocacy and supports the implementation of continental frameworks that safeguard and advance children's rights. The role holder will lead strategic engagement with critical AU bodies, particularly the African Committee of Experts on the Rights and Welfare of the Child (ACERWC). Instead, we want to build an experience that is memorable and unique – with food and drinks on the side. Our Guest Service Experts take the initiative and deliver a wide range of services to make sure that guests enjoy their meal. Whether setting tables, communicating with the kitchen, interacting and serving guests, or cleaning work areas and supplies, the Guest Service Expert makes transactions feel like part of the experience. No matter what position you are in, there are a few things that are critical to success – creating a safe workplace, following company policies and procedures, upholding quality standards, and ensuring your uniform, personal appearance, and communications are professional. Guest Service Experts will be on their feet and moving around (stand, sit, or walk for an extended time; moving over sloping, uneven, or slippery surfaces), managing the menu (read and visually verify information), and taking a hands-on approach to work (move, lift, carry, push, pull, and place objects weighing less than or equal to 25 pounds without assistance and 50 pounds with assistance; reach overhead and below the knees, including bending, twisting, pulling, and stooping). Doing all these things well (and other reasonable job duties as requested) is critical for Guest Service Experts – to get it right for our guests and our business each and every time. Preferred Qualifications Education: High school diploma or G.E.D. equivalent. Related Work Experience: Less than 1 year related work experience. Supervisory Experience: No supervisory experience.
